opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grant £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Long-Term Research); £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications); £2,500 (Research and Travel)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months) for New Projects/Commissions, Acquisitions/Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications and Long-Term Research; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for Research and Travel grants. Not for individuals developing their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing, display, conferences, lectures, non-commercial publications, long-term research, and research/travel for sculpture historians, academics and conservators. Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Artists and researchers (academics, curators, artists). Research Fellowships at the Institute for academics/curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture; fellowships at Studios & Gardens for researchers on Henry Moore specifically; Artist Research Fellowships for artists; Senior Fellowships (six weeks) for established scholars.
opportunities.summary: Month-long fellowships enabling artists and researchers to develop their work using the Henry Moore Institute's facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications currently closed for 2026/27; next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 for MA dissertation, plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, awarded to BA and MA students. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
